cands.bio: Republican candidate for Alabama House District 32. Per his campaign site, he spent 16 years as Assistant Fire Chief of Lincoln, served nine years on the Lincoln City Council, and owns GC Construction Group, a land development and general contracting business.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace. We found no record of specific votes or actions from his nine years on the Lincoln City Council, and no dates for that service. His campaign site gives general goals (responsible growth, new industry and jobs, community services, schools and job training) but no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice. We found no documented public stance on data centers or development, no controversies, no foreign ties, and no endorsements. His career details come only from his own campaign website, and no news reporting was available to confirm them.

cands.bio: Democrat elected to the Alabama House of Representatives, District 32, in the November 3, 2026 general election, defeating Republican Joey Callahan. She won the May 2026 Democratic primary over David Reddick. Her work history and background were not found in the sources available.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as endorsed or recommended by Her Bold Move, Tabitha's List, Unburdening The Ballot (Sway voting group) and YALLvote.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Debra Foster was born or raised, when she came to Alabama, or her career and work history. We found no record of prior elected office. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no stated positions on data centers, property taxes, development, immigration, guns, abortion, policing or schools. We also found no sponsored bills, official actions or news coverage of controversies.
